title: Clawd HQ: Chief of Staff Agent for Claude Code Launches
summary: Clawd HQ coordinates specialist Claude Code agents through a chief-of-staff architecture. Open-source orchestration layer launches on GitHub today.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Clawd HQ introduces a chief-of-staff architecture that coordinates multiple specialist Claude Code agents through intelligent task delegation and context management.
- The open-source tool launched on GitHub today, allowing developers to orchestrate coding agents for complex multi-step workflows without manual intervention.
- Early adopters on Hacker News highlight potential for scaling Claude Code projects by delegating subtasks to specialized agents with focused contexts.


A new orchestration tool for Claude Code brings enterprise-style task delegation to AI coding workflows. Clawd HQ, launched today on GitHub by developer Vedant Shah, implements a chief-of-staff pattern that coordinates specialist agents rather than running them independently or in sequence. The tool addresses a core challenge in agentic coding: managing context and task boundaries when multiple AI agents work on the same codebase.


## Chief-of-Staff Architecture for Agent Coordination


Clawd HQ introduces a hierarchical coordination model borrowed from executive operations. A meta-agent acts as chief of staff, analyzing incoming tasks, delegating subtasks to specialist agents, and synthesizing results. Each specialist agent operates with a focused context window, reducing token waste and improving output relevance.


The architecture contrasts with parallel or sequential agent patterns. Instead of launching multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously or chaining them in a linear pipeline, Clawd HQ dynamically assigns work based on task type. A frontend specialist handles UI changes, a backend specialist manages API logic, and a testing specialist writes unit tests, all coordinated by the chief-of-staff layer.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 23, 2026, Clawd HQ is available as an open-source repository on GitHub. Developers can clone the project and integrate it with existing Claude Code workflows today. The tool requires an Anthropic API key and supports both local and cloud-hosted Claude Code instances.


## Key Features and Use Cases


The coordination layer handles several workflow challenges that emerge in complex coding projects:


- Task decomposition: breaks high-level requests into atomic subtasks with clear ownership
- Context isolation: each specialist agent sees only relevant files and documentation
- Conflict resolution: the chief of staff mediates when agents produce incompatible changes
- Progress tracking: centralizes status updates and error handling across agents


Early use cases include refactoring legacy codebases, building full-stack features from specifications, and migrating projects between frameworks. One Hacker News commenter noted potential for scaling Claude Code projects that previously hit context limits with single-agent approaches.


## Implementation Details


Clawd HQ runs as a Python service that wraps the Claude API. The chief-of-staff agent uses a custom prompt template that includes task taxonomy, delegation heuristics, and result aggregation rules. Specialist agents receive narrower prompts with file-level context and explicit constraints.


The system maintains a shared state graph that tracks dependencies between subtasks. When a frontend change requires a new API endpoint, the chief of staff sequences the backend agent first, then passes the endpoint contract to the frontend agent. This dependency-aware scheduling prevents rework and reduces overall token consumption compared to uncoordinated multi-agent runs.


## What This Means


Clawd HQ represents a shift from monolithic AI coding sessions to orchestrated specialist teams. By applying organizational patterns to agent coordination, the tool makes complex coding workflows more manageable and cost-effective. Developers who struggle with Claude Code context limits or inconsistent multi-step outputs gain a structured alternative. As agentic coding tools mature, hierarchical coordination may become standard practice for large-scale software projects, mirroring how human engineering teams already delegate and specialize work.
